bibliography.title: Overcoming Joint Intractability with Lossless Hierarchical Speculative Decoding

sections.title: 4 Theoretical Foundations of Hierarchical Speculative Decoding
4.3 Resampling in a Hierarchy of Accessible Branches
D Expected Number of Accepted Tokens
G Integration with Recursive Reject Sampling in the Multi-Draft Setup

abstract_sentences.text: Verification is a key bottleneck in improving inference speed while maintaining distribution fidelity in Speculative Decoding.
Recent work has shown that sequence-level verification leads to a higher number of accepted tokens compared to token-wise verification.
However, existing solutions often rely on surrogate approximations or are constrained by partial information, struggling with joint intractability.

In this work, we propose Hierarchical Speculative Decoding (HSD), a provably lossless verification method that significantly boosts the expected number of accepted tokens and overcomes joint intractability by balancing excess and deficient probability mass across accessible branches.

evidence.anchor: balancing excess and deficient probability mass

abstract_sentences.text: Our extensive large-scale experiments demonstrate that HSD yields consistent improvements in acceptance rates across diverse model families and benchmarks.
Moreover, its strong explainability and generality make it readily integrable into a wide range of speculative decoding frameworks.
Notably, integrating HSD into EAGLE-3 yields over a 12% performance gain, establishing state-of-the-art decoding efficiency without compromising distribution fidelity.

final_judgment.single_storyline: HSD converts full-joint verification into branch-local divergence accounting, then uses hierarchy and capped prefix ratios to make one resample lossless and efficient (p.3–7; p.19–22).
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body keeps the failure model, Definitions 1–6, Eq. (11)–(20), Algorithms 1–2, Figure 1, GSM8K example, Tables 1–4, and EAGLE-3 qualification (p.2–10).
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Detailed proofs, A.1–A.95, seed/accuracy/capping tables, Python listings, Algorithm 3, and runtime FLOPs are in p.13–34; this preserves readability but raises proof-verification cost.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 → Eq. (4)–(10) → Eq. (16)–(20) → Tables 1–4 gives a compact object-to-guarantee-to-measurement chain (p.2–10).
final_judgment.largest_gap: There is no standalone limitations section; main tables lack uncertainty, multi-draft omits Blockwise, and EAGLE-3 BE identifiability is qualified only after the headline result (p.9–10, p.28).
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a guarantee-plus-efficiency method, expose the accessible object, conserved correction mass, single-step algorithm, proof, and identifiable experiment in that order, then state the strongest alternative explanation beside the result.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule requires a local conservation quantity and a testable output distribution; hardware-only gains or methods without accessible local states need separate systems evidence rather than a hierarchy proof (p.33–34).

formal_definitions.label: Definition 1
formal_definitions.title: Generalized Divergence
formal_definitions.description: DΩ′(p,q) sums positive target-minus-draft mass over Ω′; reverse arguments measure excess.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 2
formal_definitions.title: Branch Divergence
formal_definitions.description: DBranch(p,q|prefix) sums local positive differences over the accessible next-token branch.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 3
formal_definitions.title: Asymmetry of Branch Divergence
formal_definitions.description: ΔBranch is deficient mass minus excess mass in the current branch.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 4
formal_definitions.title: Maximum Prefix Ratio Index
formal_definitions.description: m(X1:t) is the maximizing prefix joint-ratio position, or 0 if no prefix exceeds 1.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 5
formal_definitions.title: Capped Prefix Ratio
formal_definitions.description: r* caps the last over-one prefix and keeps the suffix ratio.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 6
formal_definitions.title: Capped Branch Divergence
formal_definitions.description: D*Branch(p,q) and D*Branch(q,p) split capped positive and non-positive mass.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 7
formal_definitions.title: Sequence of Unique Capping Indices
formal_definitions.description: M* is the ordered set of unique maximum prefix-ratio indices.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 9
formal_definitions.title: Resampling Probability Mass
formal_definitions.description: Total generation mass decomposes into acceptance, unique-capping resampling, and terminal resampling.

formal_definitions.label: Definition 10
formal_definitions.title: Segmented Probability Function
formal_definitions.description: Fl is q through m*l and p thereafter, enabling telescoping.
